rows.snippet: Fifteen isolates (5.9%) produced compounds that strongly stimulated SCN egg hatch compared to PDB controls (Table 1).
rows.locator: Results, printed page 28/PDF page 6, lower left column.
rows.extraction_note: Typeset span visually checked. PDFKit splits controls across a line as con- plus trols. Plain whitespace normalization does not match; no native VERIFIED claim.
rows.assessment: Fungal isolates are the microbial actors. The study reports increased Heterodera glycines hatch relative to uninoculated potato dextrose broth. Counts include moving and immobile juveniles at 14 days, normalized to initial eggs and then control hatch. Culture age differs from exposure duration. The strong-effect reporting threshold is not a universal trait boundary. Nutrient depletion and added compounds remain alternative explanations; host, isolate and culture age matter. No common secretion mechanism, field efficacy or canonical taxon follows.
rows.inspection: Fresh USDA PDF is byte-identical to the prior article. Reread extracted Methods/Results/Discussion pages 2,3,5,6,7; visually inspected actual pages 1,3,6,7 including Figure 1. No new all-pages visual audit or complete raw-data reanalysis.

rows.snippet: When incubated with Gram-positive bacteria, only T. muris eggs showed noticeable hatching after 20 h, although with high variability.
rows.locator: Scientific Abstract, Results; full Results and Figure 2 supply comparator details.
rows.assessment: An independent bacterial experiment, not a citation of Meyer. Released larvae divided by initial embryonated eggs measures hatch. Gram-positive results at 20 h without antimicrobials are variable; Enterococcus caccae and Lactobacillus reuteri exceed bacteria-free controls. Tested T. suis groups show little hatch, not proven absolute biological inability. Antimicrobials and storage history affect interpretation. E. coli strain/concentration ANOVA excludes near-zero controls. No direct-contact mechanism, infection benefit, therapeutic use or species-wide canonical exemplar is inferred.
rows.inspection: Direct scientific Abstract, Methods, own Results, Table 1, Figure 2 and Discussion read; actual Figure 2 visually inspected. No supplement links identified in retrieved publisher anchors, and Europe PMC reports hasSuppl=N; not proof of universal supplemental absence.

allocation.scientific_scope: A physiological capability of a microorganism to increase nematode egg hatching over a defined observation interval relative to comparable controls without that microbial influence.

novelty.identity: A positive microbial hatch-enhancing capability, not the mere absence of inhibition. It need not be secretion-mediated or benefit the microorganism. Not nematode susceptibility, microbial sporulation, embryo development without emergence, attraction, killing, reversible paralysis or fungal feeding. Opposite effects under other conditions do not entail organism-level disjointness.
novelty.hierarchy: Phenotype METPO:1000059 below quality METPO:1000188. Current and pinned parent agree. Infection, nutrition, secretion, attraction, paralysis and killing are not required.
novelty.ontology: Pinned/current release and explicit editor OWL plus six TSV owners include deprecated/draft content. Only fried-egg-shaped colony METPO:1007069 and annotations/stub match; not a counterpart. Byte-verified editor conversion has 31 triples and no imports.
novelty.remote: 11 open/draft PRs, 783 nonremoved changed blobs, 587 selected upstream owners; no candidate lexical hit. Fresh heads, PR bodies and states still agree.
novelty.coupled_repair: No exact synonym, ungrounded node or same-scope parent gap found in maintained matched context. Existing exclusions remain valid.
